classification.caveat: "failed an arm for want of families" counts a frame with too few LOCAL-valid families or too few spectrum points on a side. At an allocation where the coordinate precision floor is itself refusing rungs, every frame is starved for that reason and the condition carries no information about the reference pool. Read this verdict beside the LOCAL/SPECTRUM diagnosis: it is informative only where precision is no longer the binding constraint
classification.convention: fixed in tools/v8_screen_frame_audit.py before the counts are read, keyed to registered minima (§13.15's five LOCAL-valid families, §13.13's minimum points per spectrum side). It is a reporting convention, not a scientific threshold: it admits nothing and every count it reads is printed
classification.recommendation_rule: a frame-aware screen is recommended only when the loss is MATERIAL *and* the frame label carries information the pooled label does not where the truth is known
classification.why: 5 families are promising to some frame's own screen and were not forwarded, at least §13.15's minimum of 5, while frames [0, 1, 3] failed an arm for want of families. Their downstream validity is still not identifiable; what is measured is that the loss is large enough to matter if any of it were valid

lost_cells_downstream.why: a family the pooled screen did not forward was never calibrated, so no record in this study says whether any of its rungs would have been LOCAL-valid, SPECTRUM-valid, selected as core, admitted as a backup, or useful below or above A under any frame. This audit therefore counts lost cells and never credits them with a downstream outcome

predictive_on_the_forwarded_set.rule: on the forwarded families only --- the ones every frame calibrated --- the frame-specific and the pooled screen label are each scored against the frame's realised Gate-3 verdicts. No counterfactual: both labels and the truth exist for every cell counted here

screen_shape.note: the pooled screen is a budget rule (V8_FRAME_CONDITIONING.md §5); the frame screens below are what the same production kernels say on a frame's own six topics
